topics.topic: Ownership and orchestration of listener binding, startup checks, serving barrier, handoff, and rollback
questions: Which module owns opening both listeners, withholding service until all checks pass, and closing an already opened listener when the later bind fails?

Which module owns and coordinates A17's ordered startup checks, rollback, and rule that nothing is served until all checks and listener bindings succeed, given that `configuration` is the primary owner but may not know the later `store`, `backups`, `service_access`, `owner_sessions`, or `instance_lifecycle` modules?
Which module creates and exclusively binds each listener, retains it until all startup checks pass, closes it on a later binding failure, and hands it to the corresponding surface?

judgement.why: This asks the same ownership-and-orchestration question as P2, and the relevant State 3 passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Module ownership and lifecycle of service and owner-interface listeners
quotes: Ownership is by rule, not by decision: a consumer owns exactly the rules and parts of the decision its own section below names, and the primary owner owns every rule of the decision that no other section names, except a rule this text places outside the running instance (A20, A21, A22 rule 6's "never declared again"), which no module owns.

The checks after them — the backup probe (`backups`), opening or making the store (`store`) and the listeners — are run in rule 2's order by
`instance_lifecycle`, which calls this module first.

The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the configured addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
precedent.why: The ownership rule assigns otherwise-unnamed A17 policy to primary owner `configuration`, while `instance_lifecycle` owns and performs the expressly named listener-opening mechanism.

topics.topic: Pre-serving TCP connection behavior and listener activation timing
questions: Before the final listener check succeeds, must an already opened listener reject TCP connections, accept and queue them, or accept connections while withholding every HTTP answer, and when are the two listeners activated?

quotes:
Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
   names the failed item and never its value (R0-37).
judgement.why: Whether an opened listener accepts or rejects TCP connections before serving begins is startup-flow and activation timing, not module ownership, so State 4 owns the question.
